title: ProtocolLab Package Producer Boundary Verification
verification_method: Focused template tests, release-workflow contract checks, exact candidate-package Raw QUIC conformance, package generation dry-runs, local package-backed controller execution, live lab-controller execution, touched SpecTrace JSON parse/link checks, attempted full SpecTrace validation, and diff hygiene.
scope: Verify the quic-dotnet ProtocolLab package producer boundary and the package-backed HTTP/3 1KB ProtocolLab lane. This artifact does not verify publishable benchmark provenance, broad raw QUIC support, or HTTP/3/QPACK protocol correctness beyond ProtocolLab validation and explicit HTTP/3 protocol proof for the exercised lane.
procedure: Run the H3 package producer with `-PackageTarget Http3`, a fixed package version, and `-RuntimeIdentifier linux-x64` when a sibling ProtocolLab checkout with the package builder is available.
Run the H3 package producer with `-PackageTarget Http3`, a fixed package version, and `-RuntimeIdentifier win-x64` for local bundled-worker execution.
Run `Invoke-QuicDotNetProtocolLabRun.ps1` for `http3.payload.bytes.1kb` against a local bundled controller/worker.
Run repeated local `http3.payload.bytes.1kb` H3 load-generator baselines with explicit `--repetitions` and the `h3-small-payload-c32` and `h3-small-payload-c128` load profiles.
Run `Invoke-QuicDotNetProtocolLabRun.ps1` for `http3.payload.bytes.1kb` against the live lab controller when a compatible worker is available.
Run the raw package producer with `-PackageTarget RawQuic`, a fixed package version, and `-RuntimeIdentifier linux-x64` when a sibling ProtocolLab checkout with the package builder is available.

Pack an exact `Incursa.Quic` candidate and run `scripts/release/Test-IncursaQuicPackageConformance.ps1` against an isolated ProtocolLab internal checkout with `PROTOCOL_LAB_INCURSA_QUIC_SOURCE_ROOT` absent.
Verify the candidate package SHA-256, copied server assembly SHA-256, dependency manifest package identity, 5/5 TRX result, and retained JSON summary.
Inspect produced package JSON output, package IDs, package versions, SHA-256 values, and generated manifests.
Run a touched-artifact JSON parse and reciprocal-link check for `SPEC-QUIC-INT`, `ARC-QUIC-INT-0028`, `WI-QUIC-INT-0028`, and `VER-QUIC-INT-0028`.

Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/Validate-SpecTraceJson.ps1 -RepoRoot . -Profiles core`; if the repository baseline has unrelated validation debt, preserve the failure shape separately from the package-producer evidence.
expected_result: The focused tests pass, the NuGet release workflow runs the exact package-backed Raw QUIC correctness helper before push and requires its private-fixture credential, the helper rejects source-root fallback and proves matching candidate/server assembly identities with 5/5 deterministic download and slow-reader results, H3 package generation produces `quic-dotnet-dev` with HTTP/3-only declarations including `http3.payload.bytes.1kb`, raw package generation produces `quic-dotnet-raw-dev` with only the enabled raw QUIC transport scenarios, raw H3-shaped run-helper arguments fail before upload or submission, package-backed local and live controller jobs pass validation and benchmark execution for `http3.payload.bytes.1kb`, small-payload H3 load profiles resolve to their intended local load shape, touched SpecTrace JSON parses with reciprocal links, and diff hygiene passes. Full repository SpecTrace validation should pass only when unrelated baseline validation debt is absent.

status_summary: Passed for the package producer boundary, the package-backed HTTP/3 1KB lane, and the release-time Raw QUIC package conformance contract. The release workflow now requires a read-only private-fixture credential and runs a locally packed candidate through exact package/binary provenance checks plus five deterministic correctness tests before NuGet push; it does not run BenchmarkDotNet or a ProtocolLab performance campaign. The 1KB lane is measurable as repeated local-lab evidence with explicit HTTP/3 protocol proof and c32 small-payload load-profile coverage. The c128 profile remains invalid local stress evidence that identifies the next small-payload bottleneck around managed load generation / HTTP/3 connection stability under high concurrency. These metrics remain shared-host/local-lab samples with comparability warnings and are not publishable benchmark provenance.
